name: Blacksmith's Talent
description:
When this enters, create a Sword.

{2}{R}: Level 2

At the beginning of combat on your turn, target Equipment [effect not specified] until end of turn.

{3}{R}: Level 3

Creatures you control have double strike and haste.
assumptions: Treated node D's thing: "sword" as a created permanent literally called "Sword" (worded "create a Sword"), since the node's role (enters, owner me, to bf, no flags) matches the standard token-creation pattern even though no registry entry backs it.
Did not add a "you control" restriction to the Level 2 ability's target Equipment, since node G's flags include target but no ownership qualifier — left it as a bare "target Equipment."

Assumed the Level 2/Level 3 activated abilities follow the standard "{cost}: Level N" print format, since the nodes give the cost and unlocked follow-on effects but not literal printed wording for the level-up line itself.
couldNotDerive: The Sword created at Level 1 (node D) has no corresponding entry in the labels registry, so its full type line, subtype, and stats/rules text (e.g., whether it's an Equipment, its equip cost, or any bonus it grants) cannot be determined.

Node G's cond: flag is present but empty, so the actual effect granted to the targeted Equipment by the Level 2 ability (what it "gains" or how it changes) cannot be determined — only that something happens to it, targeted, until end of turn.
notes:
Three separate, confirmed decomposition/translator gaps, all traced to app/lib/forgeTranslate.ts against forge-model/data/blacksmith-s-talent.txt's real oracle text (Blacksmith's Talent, {R} Enchantment — Class). Not a match.

1. Token's own printed abilities entirely missing. SVar:TrigToken (`DB$ Token | TokenScript$ sword | TokenOwner$ You`) creates a colorless Equipment token named Sword that itself prints "Equipped creature gets +1/+1" and "Equip {2}". TOKEN_SCRIPT_MAP (forgeTranslate.ts ~L382-396) has no entry for "sword" (only treasure/horror-1/food/bat-1/rat-1/snail-1/squirrel-1/fish-1/otter-1/wall-1/cat-1/rabbit-1), so the Token handler (ek==='Token', ~L1062-1077) falls back to the literal TokenScript string, producing node D's bare `thing:"sword"` and an unmapped `TokenScript$sword` entry. This is only half data-gap (add a `sword` labels entry) — the deeper gap is structural: the labels registry (synergy-model/data/registries.json) and the Token handler have no way to represent a created token's OWN static/activated abilities at all (no field for a token's granted keyword/static/cost), so even a correctly-registered sword entry couldn't carry "+1/+1" or "Equip {2}". The reconstruction correctly flagged this as could-not-derive but the printed card loses two whole abilities here.

2. Level 2's real effect ("attach target Equipment you control to up to one target creature you control") is completely absent. SVar:TrigPump (`DB$ Pump | ValidTgts$ Equipment.YouCtrl | ... | SubAbility$ DBAttach`) is Forge's idiom for targeting an Equipment with no P/T delta, chained into SVar:DBAttach (`DB$ Attach | Object$ ParentTarget | ValidTgts$ Creature.YouCtrl | TargetMin$ 0 | TargetMax$ 1`) which performs the actual attach. Two bugs: (a) `Attach` is not a key in EFFECT_ROLE (~L403-416) and has no dedicated `ek==='Attach'` branch anywhere in translateEffectRow — it falls into the generic no-role fallback (~L1599-1629), which only pushes an unmapped entry and drops the effect with no node at all, so the second target ("up to one target creature you control", optional per TargetMin$0/TargetMax$1) and the actual attach action never reach the graph. (b) The Pump handler (ek==='Pump', ~L1406-1451) doesn't recognize a Pump row with neither NumAtt$/NumDef$ nor KW$ as a non-effect targeting step: `hasDelta` is false and `grant` is undefined, so `cond` collapses to the literal string "cond:" (nothing after the colon) — exactly node G's flags ("target lifetime:turn cond:"). It also applies the handler's default `lifetime:turn` (since Permanent$ isn't set) even though nothing here is a real temporary stat/keyword change, fabricating a "for the turn" duration on what is actually a permanent attachment. The reconstruction, working only from this empty cond:, correctly could not derive the effect and rendered a vague, wrong "[effect not specified] until end of turn" — the real ability (attach Equipment to a creature) is nowhere in the reconstruction.

3. Level 3's ability is missing both its "equipped" restriction and its "during your turn" gate, so the reconstruction over-generalized it to all creatures you control at all times. Real: "During your turn, equipped creatures you control have double strike and haste" (SVar:SBoost: `Mode$ Continuous | Condition$ PlayerTurn | Affected$ Creature.YouCtrl+equipped | AddKeyword$ Double Strike & Haste`). Node I is `{role:modifier, thing:creature, flags:"cond:grant=double_strike;grant=haste"}` — no cond:equipped, no turn restriction. Two compounding bugs in the static AddKeyword handler: (a) `qualifierFlags()` (~L324-357) and the `equipped` boolean (~L698, `/\.(?:EquippedBy|EnchantedBy)\b/`) both only match a literal `.EquippedBy`/`.EnchantedBy` qualifier — `Affected$ Creature.YouCtrl+equipped` uses a bare `+equipped` qualifier that neither regex catches, so the restriction is dropped before it even reaches the AddKeyword branch. (b) Even where `equipped` IS detected, the AddKeyword branch (~L753-782) never consults it — only the AddPower/AddToughness branch (~L749) prefixes `equipped;` onto its cond: payload; AddKeyword's cond: is built solely from `parts.join(';')` (the keyword grants) with no equipped check at all. Separately, `Condition$ PlayerTurn` is only read inside AddKeyword's own special-case for the literal keyword 'Flying' (~L777: `kw==='Flying' && fields.Condition==='PlayerTurn' ? 'your_turn;blocked_by=flying_or_reach' : keywordGrantFact(kw)`) — for Double Strike/Haste (or any other keyword), `Condition$ PlayerTurn` is silently ignored, so "during your turn" never makes it into node I regardless of the equipped-qualifier bug. Net effect: the reconstruction's "Creatures you control have double strike and haste" is a real overstatement of the printed card (unconditional and unrestricted vs. equipped-only, your-turn-only).

All three gaps are process-error-free (the reconstructing agent read the packet as generated, correctly flagged the two it could detect as could-not-derive) and schema-capable in principle (equipped/your_turn/target-count are all expressible via existing flags — cond:equipped, cond:your_turn, TargetMin/Max qty — schema.md doesn't need new vocabulary). All three are therefore decomposition/translator bugs in app/lib/forgeTranslate.ts, not schema gaps, except the token's-own-abilities case which is a genuine schema gap (no field anywhere for a created token's own granted static/activated abilities) layered on top of the TOKEN_SCRIPT_MAP data gap.
